references.text: This verse is the opposite blessing to the curse in verse 16. While verse 3 promises blessing in the city and in the field, verse 16 promises a curse on those same places.
Continues the theme of curses over daily activities - here a curse over the basket and kneading trough, which complements the curse over the city and the field.
Cain's curse from the ground, where he becomes a fugitive and wanderer, shows the same pattern of a curse affecting both dwelling place and agriculture.
Parallel warnings about curses that follow disobedience to God's commands, including loss of blessing in the land.
Jeremiah describes a curse on the one who trusts in people rather than the Lord, with images of desert and desolate places.
Malachi speaks of how blessings will turn into curses for the priests who do not honor the Lord's name.
